source: design-spec-parity-fixtures-4c.md v4 (D2, D3, amendments A1-A4); expected outcomes written by the design's author from the in-progress REM-PARITY text, not generated from the reference
addressing: Faults are given here as physical LBAs of the named image (a filemark counts as a record); the generator records each also as (tape_file, record_index). 'failed_data_addresses' are the (tape_file_number, object_block_index) pairs given to the Recoverer as §13.1 inputs.
record_faults: Record faults (erratum set E1) name one record by tape_file and record_index. 'length' replaces it by a record of that many bytes: the original's leading bytes when shorter, the original followed by zero bytes when longer. 'byte_edits' then set bytes ('set', hex) or XOR them with a mask ('xor', hex) at 'offset' within the record; 'from', when given, is the original bytes there. For the bootstrap (tape file 0, record 0) only, 'payload' replaces the CBOR payload by one the generator builds from the original (a changed 'scheme', 'drive_compression', or the root map's 'key_order'), updating cbor_payload_len and zeroing the old tail if the length changes, and 'header_crc' and 'payload_crc' are 'recomputed', 'stale', or 'recomputed if the length changes'; absent means untouched. The edits apply in that order: length, byte edits, payload, header CRC, payload CRC. A case with 'observations' runs the reader once per observation, each with its own supplied values ('hints'), or none (null). Such a case's 'expected' maps each observation to its outcome; an expectation that reads pending, or that the executor does not know, fails the case.
erratum_e1_source: Expected outcomes of cases e1-01 to e1-15 were written from the REM-PARITY in-progress text (SHA-256 acbc31385e39af233f45769387d7bf33e9a41c38b152a9f8b1cc601c7aa85491) by an author who saw only the text and the constructions, never the reference's outcomes. Every compared field (discovery, error, field, inventory) is transcribed without change, as are the author's sections, quotes and ambiguity notes; the author's reasoning text is omitted and kept with the author's working notes. Each observation's quotes are that text's sentences; a leading bracketed locator names where an excerpt comes from.
erratum_e2_source: Expected outcomes of cases e2-01 to e2-04 were written from the REM-PARITY in-progress text (SHA-256 acbc31385e39af233f45769387d7bf33e9a41c38b152a9f8b1cc601c7aa85491) by an author who saw only the text and the catalogue's constructions, never the reference's outcomes. Each case's expected object is the author's entry, transcribed without change (result, error, sections, quotes, and the component, classification, map and open notes where given). The executor compares the author's error and the leading clause of the result through a closed vocabulary; an unknown clause fails the case. read_data_addresses are the Object addresses a Recoverer, given the tape and its validated terminal inventory, is asked for: the executor reads them through the production object source, which meets the record fault itself.

Its stripe has one erasure (lost_count 1 ≤ m = 2). The block is reconstructed from the first k = 2 trusted shards: the data shard at ordinal 2, address (1, 2), and parity (stripe 0, parity_index 0) at sidecar block H + 0·S + 0 = 1. It is verified against its sidecar data CRC and released identical to the original. This is not TapeIo.

cases.note: Observation (catalogue E2): a Scanner with no off-tape state.

expected.result: inventory returned, degraded. Walking back from EOD, the Scanner reads C's footer first. A record longer than one block is an invalid candidate for a control component, so it supplies no planned layout. BC's separation footer is not a replica footer. B's footer parses at its recorded position, with planned EOD equal to the tape's EOD, and supplies the layout. Validating the three planned replicas: C fails Section 10.6's record-length condition, while A and B validate and agree. The Scanner accepts A or B (which one is the Guide's selection order) and reports the inventory as degraded because C is invalid. There is no conflict, and this is not TapeIo. As a component, C is TerminalIndexReplicaParse.

A terminal replica's footer that parses supplies a planned layout only when its recorded footer position equals the position at which it was read, and the layout's planned EOD is at or after the tape's EOD.

validate the header, footer and trailing filemark of every replica that layout plans; a replica's payload need be validated only for the replica to be accepted, or when two replica envelopes differ in an edition-common field;
before accepting any replica, consider every replica that validates for conflict under Section 8.5;

fault.unreadable: every record of all three terminal replicas

expected.result: BotStructuralRecoveryRequired, and the walk produces a map that is validated against the final ParityMap. Terminal authority is reported as not recovered.
quotes: A terminal replica's footer that parses supplies a planned layout only when its recorded footer position equals the position at which it was read, and the layout's planned EOD is at or after the tape's EOD.
A magic or CRC miss invalidates that candidate. A medium error invalidates the affected candidate, while a non-medium transport error aborts discovery.
if no replica validates, perform the BOT structural recovery walk in Section 8.4.1.

If A, B, and C all fail, the Scanner returns an explicit `BotStructuralRecoveryRequired` outcome and performs the Section 8.4.1 walk; BOT Object classifications are likewise streamed before their terminal summary.
When A, B, and C are all absent or invalid, the Scanner MUST offer a full structural walk from BOT.

The walk reconstructs tape-file boundaries, validates recognisable ParitySidecar and control structure, and measures complete Object candidates by elimination. It reports each candidate's identity as unknown unless a separate exact Object-recovery authority succeeds.
The Scanner MUST report that terminal authority was not recovered.

Per tape file: read the head block; measure the file's length by filemark spacing (space to the next filemark; the file's block count is the position delta minus one); a zero-block file or a missing trailing filemark is structural damage; EOD at a file start ends the walk.

A Reader treats it as invalid content of the component it belongs to: an invalid candidate for a control component, an erasure when the Recoverer reads a data block or parity shard (Section 13.4), and, for the first record with a supplied or known block size, the refusal of Sections 8.4 and 15.
It is never `TapeIo`, which is reserved for a transport or medium failure and for the device reports that Section 2.4 names.
**Object, by elimination** — never by reading object content.

**Unreadable head block:** the Scanner MUST NOT abort. It MUST measure the file by filemark spacing, run the footer/tail sidecar probe, and otherwise classify the file as an object candidate. The last block it reads for that probe also serves the terminal footer probe of items 2 and 3.
When the head is unreadable, a matching, fully parsed terminal footer establishes the same type, after its measured count is checked.
**IndexSeparationExtent**: matching separation-header magic commits the tape file to this control type under the same malformed-control and measured count rules.

After the walk, when the tape's final ParityMap validates and is marked `is_final_directory`, the Scanner MUST perform a second pass that identifies as a sidecar each Object candidate at a tape file a directory entry names whose measured length equals the entry's `sidecar_total_block_count`.

A map produced by the Section 8.4.1 walk, after the second pass of Section 12.3, is validated against the tape's final ParityMap when that ParityMap validates and is marked `is_final_directory`, and the map's canonical projection (Section 7.3) through the ParityMap's own entry hashes to its `canonical_map_digest`.
The validated scope and durable boundary are the first `directory_scope_tape_file_count` tape files, ending with that ParityMap's entry; `W` is `directory_scope_highest_protected_ordinal`.

classification.1: Object candidate by elimination (item 7), 4 blocks by filemark spacing (a record longer than one block is one logical position), first_parity_data_ordinal 0, identity unknown. The 524288-byte head record is invalid content, not a refusal: the refusal of Sections 8.4 and 15 applies only to the tape's first record. The walk does not abort and does not report TapeIo. The last-block probe finds a data block, not a footer.
classification.4: replica A with every record unreadable: no magic can match and the footer probe reads nothing, so it is an Object candidate by elimination (items 7 and 'unreadable head block'), 3 blocks, outside the validated scope
classification.5: IndexSeparationExtent (item 3), committed by header magic, measured count as planned
classification.6: replica B, as file 4: Object candidate, 3 blocks, outside the validated scope
classification.8: replica C, as file 4: Object candidate, 3 blocks, outside the validated scope

silent: **Unreadable head block:** the Scanner MUST NOT abort. It MUST measure the file by filemark spacing, run the footer/tail sidecar probe, and otherwise classify the file as an object candidate. The last block it reads for that probe also serves the terminal footer probe of items 2 and 3.
When the head is unreadable, a matching, fully parsed terminal footer establishes the same type, after its measured count is checked.
A structural artifact after the exact terminal suffix is nonconformant and MUST NOT be admitted as an Object.

A Reader treats it as invalid content of the component it belongs to: an invalid candidate for a control component, an erasure when the Recoverer reads a data block or parity shard (Section 13.4), and, for the first record with a supplied or known block size, the refusal of Sections 8.4 and 15.
open.note: The text gives the walk no way to type a wholly unreadable terminal replica, so the ladder makes it an Object candidate, even though the readable separation extents plan files 4, 6 and 8 as replicas. Section 12.6's bar on admitting Objects applies only after the terminal suffix. Separately, 'the first record with a supplied or known block size' could be misread as the head of every tape file.
